Surface Water
Water Quality Monitoring — A surface water monitoring network has been operated by Westmoreland Resources since 1973. The monitoring program was established to aid in the surveillance of present mining operations on Tract III. Additional mining operations on other parts of Tract III or on Tract II will require a similar surveillance network established by the mine operator and appropriate State agencies. Westmoreland Resources has stated its intentions of continuing its monitoring network through all phases of operations on Tract III and of expanding its network in Tract II when mining operations begin.
Sediment Control - Prior to the initiation of mining operations within the boundaries of particular local drainages, water control facilities will be installed at a location downstream from the mining activity. Each facility will consist of dam and detention pond. Water will flow into these ponds through natural channels and man-made diversions. The primary purpose of these facilities is to hold runoff water which may be of low physical and chemical quality until it can meet State and Federal water quality standards and be released downstream.
Siltation from coal surface mining in flat to rolling terrain is less acute than from mining operations in mountainous regions (Grim and Hill, 1974). The most positive controls consist of proper pre-mining planning and the use of improved mining practices and modern reclamation techniques. By the development and implementation of erosion and sediment control plans before, during, and after mining, erosion can be minimized (Grim and Hill, 1974).
